utf8formatter-direct-formatting.title: Format values directly into UTF-8 buffers
utf8formatter-direct-formatting.short: Avoid temporary strings when writing formatted values to byte-oriented output
utf8formatter-direct-formatting.summary: Utf8Formatter can write common values directly into a Span<byte>, which is useful on measured serialization and protocol hot paths.
utf8formatter-direct-formatting.why: Direct formatting can remove temporary strings and encoding work when the destination is already UTF-8 bytes.
utf8formatter-direct-formatting.tips: Use it where profiling shows formatting allocations matter; ordinary interpolation remains clearer for non-hot code.

gc-latency-modes-tradeoffs.title: Choose GC latency modes by pause and throughput needs
gc-latency-modes-tradeoffs.short: Treat low-latency GC settings as a scoped runtime tradeoff
gc-latency-modes-tradeoffs.summary: GC latency modes change how aggressively the runtime prioritizes shorter pauses versus collection efficiency and memory pressure.
gc-latency-modes-tradeoffs.why: A latency setting chosen without workload measurements can trade one kind of pause for higher memory use or lower throughput.
gc-latency-modes-tradeoffs.tips: Measure representative workloads, keep unusual modes scoped, and restore changed process-wide settings when appropriate.

httpclient-pooled-connection-lifetime.title: Bound pooled HTTP connection lifetime when endpoints can change
httpclient-pooled-connection-lifetime.short: Reuse HttpClient while allowing long-lived connections to refresh
httpclient-pooled-connection-lifetime.summary: SocketsHttpHandler can retire pooled connections after a configured lifetime so later requests establish fresh connections.
httpclient-pooled-connection-lifetime.why: Long-lived clients need connection reuse, but indefinitely retained connections can keep using stale endpoint resolution in some deployments.
httpclient-pooled-connection-lifetime.tips: Choose a lifetime based on DNS and service-discovery behavior rather than recreating HttpClient per request.

lazy-thread-safety-publication.title: Choose Lazy<T> publication semantics deliberately
lazy-thread-safety-publication.short: Match initialization behavior to duplicate-work and exception requirements
lazy-thread-safety-publication.summary: Lazy<T> thread-safety modes determine whether initialization is serialized and which produced value becomes published under concurrency.
lazy-thread-safety-publication.why: The wrong mode can introduce duplicate expensive work or unnecessary locking around initialization.
lazy-thread-safety-publication.tips: Prefer the default ExecutionAndPublication unless duplicate construction is explicitly safe and worthwhile.

json-typeinforesolver-contract-customiza.title: Customize System.Text.Json contracts with type info resolvers
json-typeinforesolver-contract-customiza.short: Centralize metadata-based serialization policy without decorating every model
json-typeinforesolver-contract-customiza.summary: TypeInfoResolver and modifiers can adjust generated or reflection-based JSON contracts before serialization uses them.
json-typeinforesolver-contract-customiza.why: Cross-cutting naming, property, or polymorphism rules can be expressed in one policy layer instead of scattered model attributes.
json-typeinforesolver-contract-customiza.tips: Keep modifiers deterministic and test interactions with source-generated metadata and polymorphic contracts.

memorycache-eviction-callback-work.title: Keep MemoryCache eviction callbacks lightweight
memorycache-eviction-callback-work.short: Move slow cleanup away from cache callback paths
memorycache-eviction-callback-work.summary: Eviction callbacks are useful for observing removal, but expensive cleanup inside them can couple cache maintenance to unrelated work.
memorycache-eviction-callback-work.why: Blocking or CPU-heavy callback work can create latency spikes and surprising contention during bursts of eviction.
memorycache-eviction-callback-work.tips: Capture only necessary state and hand substantial cleanup to a bounded background mechanism.

async-dispose-concurrent-use.title: Stop concurrent users before asynchronous disposal
async-dispose-concurrent-use.short: Treat DisposeAsync as a lifetime boundary, not a race with active operations
async-dispose-concurrent-use.summary: Asynchronous disposal may release resources over time, but callers must still coordinate ownership so active operations do not use an object while it is being torn down.
async-dispose-concurrent-use.why: Concurrent use and disposal can produce intermittent failures, corrupted protocol state, or use-after-dispose behavior.
async-dispose-concurrent-use.tips: Define one owner, stop new work, await in-flight work when required, then dispose exactly once.

socket-partial-send-receive.title: Handle partial socket sends and receives
socket-partial-send-receive.short: Do not assume one socket operation transfers an entire application message
socket-partial-send-receive.summary: Stream sockets expose a byte stream, so send and receive operations may complete after transferring fewer bytes than requested.
socket-partial-send-receive.why: Assuming message-sized completion can truncate output or parse incomplete input under normal network conditions.
socket-partial-send-receive.tips: Loop over remaining bytes and define explicit framing for application messages.

linq-multiple-enumeration-expensive-sour.title: Avoid accidental repeated enumeration of expensive LINQ sources
linq-multiple-enumeration-expensive-sour.short: Remember that a query can execute again each time it is enumerated
linq-multiple-enumeration-expensive-sour.summary: Deferred LINQ sequences may repeat database, file, generator, or CPU work when inspected and then enumerated again.
linq-multiple-enumeration-expensive-sour.why: A harmless-looking Any, Count, or logging pass can duplicate expensive work or observe different data.
linq-multiple-enumeration-expensive-sour.tips: Know the source semantics; enumerate once, materialize deliberately when reuse is required, or use a source-specific existence query.

unity-native-container-disposal.title: Dispose Unity native containers according to allocator lifetime
unity-native-container-disposal.short: Make ownership of persistent native memory explicit
unity-native-container-disposal.summary: NativeArray and related native containers can own unmanaged memory whose lifetime is not governed by the managed garbage collector.
unity-native-container-disposal.why: Missing disposal can leak native memory across scenes or long editor sessions, while early disposal can invalidate jobs still using the data.
unity-native-container-disposal.tips: Match allocator choice to lifetime, complete dependent jobs before disposal, and centralize ownership.
